correctness.rationale: Invariant covariance gives the exact rank-dependent kernel and centered second moment. Uniqueness of the invariant projection follows by compact-group averaging and the one-dimensional stabilizer-fixed matrix space, proving its minimal norm. The fixed-k chi-square limit and growing k=o(sqrt(n)) normal limit follow from Jiang (arxiv:math/0601457, Theorem 1), with exact second moments ensuring uniform integrability. Direct gamma integration gives the coefficient, a strictly positive integral for the digamma difference proves all-rank monotonicity, and Stirling gives the limiting coefficient. Checker recomputed beta-integral cases and Haar second moments, but finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The claim identifies an all-rank family of exact minimal projection norm formulas on real Grassmannians and strictly increasing fixed-rank asymptotic constants plus a sparse-growing-rank limit. Jiang provides the distributional block approximation and Defant et al. concern spherical polynomial projections. The published source inspections and current record searches identified no theorem from either that already entails the full rank-profile statement. The rank-one case is expressly acknowledged as prior work; an unindexed or implicit stronger theorem is a material residual risk.

value.rationale: A sharp operator/projection constant for a full canonical family of continuous homogeneous manifolds is mathematically motivated; the strict fixed-rank hierarchy, exact minimality, and growing-sparse-rank universality distinguish geometry across infinitely many rank families. The result isolates a meaningful unresolved critical window rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The k=1 beta identity is an established comparison, not itself the asserted contribution.
